newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-U.S. Sept bonds retrench, bulls downcast.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-U.S. Sept bonds retrench, bulls downcast.

text.p: The bullish mood in the U.S. T-bond futures market was slightly dampened after September retrenched to 113-20/32 from a seven-month high of 114-03/32, technical analysts and traders said.
Two U.S. institutions sold a total of 3,000 contracts which yanked September from its newly established seven-month high towards a short-term technical level of 113-25/32.
"Because it traded as low as it did, it really dampened my outlook which was quite bullish at the opening," a T-bond futures analyst said.
Most traders said September bonds were still bullish above Tuesday's low of 113-12/32.
"I'm looking for a top, and this may be it," said Steven Poser, senior technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "If it turns much lower, odds are this is a (short-term) top."

Many technical analysts and traders were looking for September T-bonds to rise to 114-08/32, a 75 percent retracement level. Some expected September to hit 114-16/32 as early as Wednesday afternoon. At that point, they were looking for the contract to correct as much as two points.
Michael Zentz, Treasury market strategist at FX Concepts, said 114-16/32 is an upside target measured from September's base of 105-30/32 on April 11 to the 110-00 area in mid-May.

"On a longer-term basis, the whole move from 105-30/32 to about 110-10/32 was a base," Zentz said. "We broke above that base. We've had one scare to the downside, but other than that the corrections have been pretty mild since April."
Zentz said a pullback to 113-08/32 to 113-03/32 would draw in long positions.
"There are plenty of bulls, but I think there are some people hoping for a pullback," he said.
According to his cyclical studies, the U.S. T-bond futures market is not expected to top until the week of July 21. ((Chicago derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
